messages:
alex: FYI — hit a prod regression yesterday where a cold-start surge caused a bunch of requests to fall back to CPU. Looks like prefetch aborted. Anyone seen this exact trace?

maya: saw a variant on canary. Prefetch returns ENOSPACE then we timeout waiting for contiguous staging.

simon: can you dump the allocator decision trace? need to know whether we failed contiguity vs global free.

alex: pasted gist of trace: 
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] prefetch: want=64MB pool=staging-numa0 try=1 -> ENOSPACE
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] prefetch: try=2 -> ENOSPACE
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] prefetch: try=3 -> TIMED_OUT
[2024-06-15T21:10:12Z] alloc: fallback to host-copy, route=immediate

jen: we should be explicit about failure classes: contiguous_fragmentation, transient_host_pressure, allocator_rate_limit. Each needs a different mitigation.

noah: infra telemetry shows host free drop ~12% concurrent with spike. So both frag + pressure plausible.

maya: important distinction: fragmentation means large contiguous chunk not available even if total free >= request. Retrying identical allocation won't help.

simon: propose algorithmic change: before declare fail, attempt scatter-prefetch (split into N smaller allocations) and reassemble in KV cache. If that fails, then try reduced-window prefetch (smaller total bytes). Only after those fail do immediate host-copy fallback.

alex: API change needed — current alloc.prefetch() returns bool. We should extend to return structured reason/strategy info, backwards compatible via opt-in flag (prefetch_v2).

jen: metric additions: prefetch_attempts_total, prefetch_failure_mode (labels: frag|pressure|throttle), prefetch_scatter_attempts, prefetch_scatter_success, largest_free_chunk_bytes_at_prefetch, host_free_pct_at_prefetch, prefetch_reassembly_latency_ms, prefetch_fallback_to_host_count.

noah: also add allocator histogram sample of largest_free_chunk_bytes. That will show contiguity trends.

ci-bot: test flakiness detected: prefetch-scatter-integration.test failed 3/10 runs; timeout during reassembly on CI.

jen: we should add deterministic shard ordering in reassembly and a unit test that simulates interleaved frees/allocs to reproduce race. Use seeded RNGs to keep CI deterministic.

maya: KV reassembly contract needs clarity: do we accept out-of-order pieces? How do we expose partial readiness to request pipeline? We probably need an ordered reassembly API or a completed-when-all-pieces-ready signal.

simon: implementation plan: 1) add prefetch_v2 opt-in + richer return struct; 2) implement scatter allocator path inside staging pool allocator; 3) implement KV reassembly buffer with piece checksums and piece-level readiness signals; 4) metrics + largest_free_chunk sample; 5) tests + canary rollout.

alex: rollout plan: enable prefetch_v2=false by default on main; land code with feature flag; run on canary (single region) for 72h; monitor prefetch_fallback_to_host_count and reassembly time; then ramp to 20% traffic if stable.

noah: safety gates: circuit-breaker to disable scatter if host_free_pct < 20% or prefetch_reassembly_latency_p95 > SLO. Also rate-limit scatter attempts per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbours.

jen: also add a cheap short-circuit: if largest_free_chunk_bytes >= request then do normal contiguous alloc; only try scatter when largest_free_chunk < request. That saves overhead.

alex: testing checklist: unit allocator tests simulating fragmentation, integration test for reassembly under concurrency, load test that spikes cold starts and asserts tail-latencies, and canary observability dashboards.

ci-bot: note: avoid touching hotpath allocations in same commit as reassembly to reduce fallout. Split into two PRs if possible.

simon: will prototype the allocator scatter path in a small standalone crate/dir so we can iterate tests without touching main runtime.

maya: KV side: we need to ensure cache invalidation semantics don't change. Reassembly must produce the exact same logical prefix bytes as contiguous prefetch. Guarantee strict equivalence or fail the prefetch.

alex: action owners: simon -> RFC + prototype; jen -> metrics + CI tests; noah -> host_free telemetry + dashboard; maya -> kvcache reassembly contract; alex -> canary rollout plan and gating.

jen: last thought: consider adaptive chunk sizing: pick chunk sizes based on sampled largest_free_chunk to reduce number of pieces. E.g., if largest_free_chunk is 20MB, split 64MB into 3x ~20MB rather than 8x 8MB.

simon: good idea. We'll use largest_free_chunk to pick chunk_target = max(min_chunk, largest_free_chunk * 0.9) and then ceil-split. Adds a step but reduces reassembly ops.

noah: I'll mock dashboard correlating largest_free_chunk vs prefetch_fallback_to_host_count to validate heuristics.

alex: thanks everyone. Simon, ping this thread when you have an RFC sketch. We'll iterate before landing. :rocket:
